chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

"When you accept land with the goodwill of its people on a condition, you must stipulate with them regarding it, for you shall have all the surplus in its cultivation if you fulfill [your obligations] to them. And if you repair a repair in it and build a structure in it, you shall have the reward of its houses, except what is in the hands of its landowners."

key_terms.بِطِيبِ نَفْسِ أَهْلِهَا: With the goodwill/consent of its people

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a cultivator regarding surplus produce and improvements in Islamic land partnership?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *muzara'ah* (sharecropping), emphasizing that the cultivator's entitlement to surplus produce and improvements is contingent upon fulfilling agreed terms with the landowners. It specifically distinguishes between general improvements, which belong to the cultivator, and structures retained by the *dehqans* (landed gentry), reflecting the socio-economic dynamics of early Shia jurisprudence. The ruling underscores the importance of mutual consent (*bi-tayyib nafs*) and contractual clarity in agricultural partnerships.
